questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: When choosing where to study it was important to me that the education was in English as well as being a country with a distinctly different culture and history to that of Denmark. Personally, Singapore was the perfect fit for this as English is the main language spoken in most settings and the culture is heavily influenced by Asian values. Moreover Singapores geographical location makes it easy to travel to other countries doing the semester.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Before arriving I had the general information I needed in order to check in to my accommodation. Generally, it is very easy to find information, but if they are very helpful over email.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had the housing office help me with how to check in, which made the process very easy.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There are halls of residence, houses, residential colleges and student residences.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Halls and colleges have meal plans whereas the others do not, but they have food courts nearby and a shared kitchen.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
It can be hard to understand the differences between the different types of accommodation, to my understanding: Halls are very social and have a lot of activities, luckily as you are an exchange student you do not have to participate in it if you do not wish to. Colleges have less activities run by the foundation but you usually live with more people, which also can create a sense of community. Student residences are not very sociable and are essentially just rooms with a shared kitchen. Houses are kind of a mix between student residences and halls, so they have a bit more social commitment. 
During the accommodation process they can make it seem like it is extremely hard to get accommodation on campus, but almost all of the people I know got on-campus accommodation.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: When you apply for NUS you will simultaneously be applying for eight courses. You'll need around four courses to fulfill the requirements, and depending on the allocation process you will already have a spot on some of your courses. In the beginning of the semester you have the opportunity to apply for additional courses, change courses and appeal if you did not get the courses you wanted.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: They provide very good manuals which you can download on their website as to when you need to apply for your courses and when the appeal process begins and ends.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got three out of the four courses I wanted, after that, I just applied for other courses that did not interfere with my schedule. Due to limited spots, I had to appeal, which was a very easy process with staff guiding you through.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: When registering i think it is a very good idea to look at the vacancy reports, that way you get an idea of how likely you will be in securing the courses.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The levels are indicated inthe thausands so three-thousand courses take more than two-thousand courses. Overall i did not find it particular harder than courses back home, there is just a bit more responsibility during the semester and not just at finals.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I had a lot of smaller seminar courses where we were only around twenty students in total which made it a bit more relaxed. Moreover, most courses have tutorials that can be helpful for discussions and understanding. The workload is very different from what I'm used to. At NUS there are different academic components throughout the year that count towards your final grade. This usually consists of group presentations and assignments.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: I was enrolled in SC2220 Gender Studies, SC3203 Race and Ethnic Relations, SC2205 Sociology of Family, and SC3228 Senses and Society.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend to enroll in the Gender Studies class as it is a broad topic that most people can follow. The tutorials are really interesting as they are discussion-based where everyone can participate. Moreover, there is no final exam for this course which makes the exam season less stressful.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I did not experience any unexpected costs during my stay, however it is nice to know that buses on campus are free.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Eating out can be very cheap if you go to the right places! Eat at hawker centers and you can get a meal for 3-5SGD. Otherwise, food at restaurants and groceries can be pretty expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is a very wide range of different clubs around campus and by the different halls. I recommend going to their CCA meetings in the beginning of the semester, there you can here all the different activities there are. I personally did NUS boxing and Raffles (my hall) swimming.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I think doing most beginner sports here is really fun as it is a bit more chill and not too competitive. However, I do recommend finding out which teams are more competition-based or more for leisure.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: In the beginning I recommend just being a tourist in Singapore and going around the city. A lot of Singaporeans go to JB during the weekends as it is very cheap there. During the longer weekends i recommend going to places such as Malaysia, Indonesia or Hongkong. For longer breaks you can go to a wide range of other countries in Asia.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy. I do not feel that there are cultural differences that are hard to overcome.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I recommend signing up for the NUS Buddy system if you want to get a Singaporean friend. I also recommend staying in a hall if you want a more submersive experience. Moreover, most locals are really nice and will be very welcoming to you. But I would say that generally, people hang out with other exchangers more than locals.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: What I found most challenging is the very high surveillance there is. Of course, it can make you feel way more safe in the country, but it is also crazy to know that you are always being surveilanced.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really appreciate how familiar the culture is in the sense that people are really welcoming and take you ‘in'. I think it depends on who you hang out with and where you end up living, but the people at my hall where very inviting.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
NUS is known for being very hard, and it can be very hard, but you do not need to stress too much about it as you just need to pass. 
There will be more work throughout the semester but then the finals count for less.
On-campus accommodation is a god sent for making friends and doing different club activities.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
NUS's website contains so much information and is extremely helpful in the beginning, so take a good look at it. 
When registering for courses at the beginning of the semester check when the exams are so they do not overlap and if they are very late in the semester.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Definitely getting to know so many new people and making very good friends with people from all over the globe. And getting to travel around Asia with these newfound friends.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I think becoming at ease with the sense of homesickness you can experience can be hard at times, but there are also so many things going on that you can hardly keep up with people back home, which also can be challenging. Overall I do not think that there were any challenges too hard to overcome.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
